text: This Master Circular is issued to enable Investment Advisers and other market stakeholders to access applicable circulars relating to Investment Advisers at one place. It incorporates the provisions of circulars listed in its appendix.

The Master Circular states that directions and instructions contained in the circulars listed in its Appendix stand rescinded to the extent that they relate to Investment Advisers, subject to the stated transitional provisions.
A person shall not act as an investment adviser unless the person has obtained a certificate of registration from the Board, subject to the applicable regulatory framework.
An investment adviser shall carry out risk profiling of the client and obtain the necessary information required for providing suitable investment advice.
An investment adviser shall ensure that investment advice is suitable to the client based on the client's risk profile and relevant circumstances.
An investment adviser shall maintain the records relating to its activities and comply with applicable record-maintenance requirements.
An investment adviser is required to enter into an agreement with the client containing the applicable terms and conditions governing the advisory relationship.
The investment adviser must provide clients with applicable information concerning fees and charges associated with investment advisory services in accordance with the regulatory requirements.
Investment advisers are required to identify and appropriately address conflicts of interest and make applicable disclosures to clients.
Investment advisers must comply with the applicable advertisement and communication requirements, including prescribed disclosures and restrictions on misleading communications.
Investment Advisers are required to comply with the general obligations applicable to them under the SEBI regulatory framework.
An Investment Adviser is required to maintain appropriate records relating to its investment advisory activities and comply with applicable record-keeping requirements.
Investment Advisers must comply with applicable provisions of the SEBI Act, regulations, circulars and directions governing investment advisory activities.
Investment Advisers are required to undertake risk profiling of their clients before providing investment advice, in accordance with applicable regulatory requirements.
Risk profiling should take into account relevant information about the client as required under the applicable regulatory framework.
The Investment Adviser should maintain records of the client's risk profile and the basis on which the profile was determined.
Investment advice provided to a client should be suitable to the client's risk profile and other relevant circumstances.
An Investment Adviser should consider the client's investment objectives, risk appetite and other relevant factors while providing investment advice.

section: Regulation 17 – Advice based on client profile
text: Investment advice should be provided only after considering the information obtained through the applicable client profiling and suitability process.
Investment advice should be provided in accordance with the applicable regulatory requirements and with due consideration of the client's interests.
An Investment Adviser is required to make the disclosures to clients prescribed under the applicable regulatory framework.
Relevant information that may reasonably affect a client's decision regarding investment advice should be disclosed in accordance with applicable requirements.
An Investment Adviser is required to disclose applicable conflicts of interest and relevant information concerning its advisory activities to clients.
Applicable fees and consideration charged by an Investment Adviser should be disclosed to the client in accordance with the regulatory requirements.
Where advisory services relate to products or services outside the regulatory purview of SEBI, the Investment Adviser is required to disclose this fact to the client.

For advisory services relating to products or services outside SEBI's regulatory purview, the client should be informed that recourse from SEBI may not be available for grievances relating to those services.
An Investment Adviser is required to disclose to the client the extent of use of Artificial Intelligence tools in providing investment advice, where applicable.
Investment Advisers are required to maintain records relating to their investment advisory activities as prescribed under the applicable regulatory requirements.
Records maintained by an Investment Adviser should include the client and advisory-related information required under the applicable regulatory framework.
Investment Advisers are required to preserve applicable records for the period and in the manner prescribed by the regulatory framework.
Investment Advisers are required to comply with the applicable requirements governing advertisements and communications relating to investment advisory services.
Communications issued by an Investment Adviser should comply with applicable requirements and should not contain information that is misleading to clients or investors.
Performance-related information used in communications by an Investment Adviser must comply with the applicable regulatory requirements.
Communications relating to investment advisory services should contain applicable risk disclosures and should not present investment outcomes without the required context.
Investment Advisers are required to maintain records relating to advertisements and communications as required under the applicable regulatory framework.
Investment Advisers are required to comply with the applicable code of conduct prescribed under the regulatory framework.
An Investment Adviser should maintain high standards of integrity, fairness and professional conduct while providing investment advisory services.
An Investment Adviser should act with due skill, care and diligence while providing investment advice to clients.
An Investment Adviser should place appropriate consideration on the interests of clients while providing investment advisory services.
An Investment Adviser should not make statements or provide information that misrepresents its services, qualifications, experience or investment advice.

An Investment Adviser should maintain appropriate confidentiality regarding client information and should not disclose such information except where permitted or required under applicable requirements.
An Investment Adviser should deal fairly with clients and should not engage in practices that may adversely affect the interests of clients.
An Investment Adviser should identify and appropriately manage conflicts of interest that may arise in providing investment advisory services.
An Investment Adviser should provide investment advice based on appropriate analysis and should not allow undisclosed interests to improperly influence the advice provided to clients.
An Investment Adviser should exercise due diligence and conduct appropriate analysis before providing investment advice to clients.
An Investment Adviser should enter into the applicable client agreement before providing investment advisory services, as required under the regulatory framework.
The client agreement should contain the applicable terms and conditions governing the investment advisory relationship.
Investment Advisers should disclose applicable fees and charges to clients in accordance with the regulatory requirements before charging them.
Fees charged by an Investment Adviser should remain within the applicable regulatory limits and conditions prescribed for investment advisory services.
An Investment Adviser should collect fees from clients in the manner and subject to the conditions prescribed under the applicable regulatory framework.
Where fees are collected in advance, the Investment Adviser should comply with the applicable conditions and requirements governing such fee collection.
An Investment Adviser should comply with applicable requirements relating to refund of fees where advisory services are discontinued or otherwise become subject to refund provisions.
An Investment Adviser should disclose material conflicts of interest that may affect the advisory services provided to clients.
Conflicts of interest arising in the course of providing investment advice should be identified and appropriately managed in accordance with applicable requirements.
An Investment Adviser should not handle or receive client funds or securities except where specifically permitted under the applicable regulatory framework.
An Investment Adviser should comply with applicable restrictions concerning the handling of client securities in connection with investment advisory services.
Investment advisory activities should be appropriately segregated from other activities where segregation is required under the applicable regulatory framework.
Where applicable, Investment Advisers should ensure that clients are able to access direct plans of mutual fund schemes in accordance with the regulatory requirements.
Investment advisory activities should comply with applicable restrictions concerning receipt of commission or other consideration from distribution activities.
Information provided by an Investment Adviser to clients should be accurate, clear and consistent with applicable regulatory requirements.
Investment Advisers are required to undergo periodic compliance audits in accordance with the applicable regulatory requirements.
The Investment Adviser should ensure that the applicable compliance audit report is prepared and submitted or maintained in the manner prescribed by SEBI.
Investment Advisers are required to submit periodic reports to the applicable regulatory authority in the format and within the timelines prescribed by SEBI.
Investment Advisers are required to make the applicable Investor Charter available to clients and comply with the disclosure requirements associated with it.
Investment Advisers are required to provide applicable information relating to investor complaints and grievance redressal on their website or other prescribed platforms.
Investment Advisers should provide clients with information about the applicable grievance redressal mechanisms, including the SEBI SCORES platform where prescribed.
An Investment Adviser should maintain the disclosures and information required under the applicable regulatory framework on its website.
The Investment Adviser should display its applicable SEBI registration details and other prescribed information on its website.

document_title: Ease of Doing Investment (EoDI)- Disclosure of registered name and registration number by SEBI regulated entities and their agents on Social Media Platforms (SMPs)
text: SEBI-regulated entities and their agents are required to comply with applicable requirements regarding disclosure of registered name and registration number on social media platforms.
An Investment Adviser is required to obtain prior approval from SEBI for a change in control where such approval is required under the applicable regulatory framework.

document_title: Reserve Bank of India (Digital Lending) Directions, 2025
section: Para 5 – Due diligence requirements with respect to LSPs
text: Digital lending involving an LSP must operate under a contract clearly defining the respective roles, rights and obligations of the RE and LSP.

document_title: Reserve Bank of India (Digital Lending) Directions, 2025
section: Para 5 – Due diligence requirements with respect to LSPs
text: Before engaging an LSP for digital lending, the RE must conduct enhanced due diligence covering technical capability, data privacy and storage systems, fairness of conduct, past conduct, and ability to comply with applicable law.

document_title: Reserve Bank of India (Digital Lending) Directions, 2025
section: Para 5 – Due diligence requirements with respect to LSPs
text: The RE must periodically review the LSP's conduct against the contractual agreement and take appropriate action for deviations.

document_title: Reserve Bank of India (Digital Lending) Directions, 2025
section: Para 5 – Due diligence requirements with respect to LSPs
text: The RE must maintain suitable monitoring mechanisms for portfolios originated with LSP support, guide LSP recovery agents appropriately, and remains fully responsible and liable for LSP acts and omissions.

document_title: Reserve Bank of India (Digital Lending) Directions, 2025
section: Para 5 – Due diligence requirements with respect to LSPs
text: The RE must continue to comply with applicable outsourcing requirements and ensure that its LSPs and their DLAs comply with the Digital Lending Directions.

document_title: Reserve Bank of India (Digital Lending) Directions, 2025
section: Para 6 – RE-LSP arrangements involving multiple lenders
text: Where an LSP works with multiple REs, it must provide a digital view of matching loan offers and disclose the names of unmatched lenders.

document_title: Reserve Bank of India (Digital Lending) Directions, 2025
section: Para 6 – RE-LSP arrangements involving multiple lenders
text: The LSP must use a consistent approach for similarly placed borrowers and products and document the mechanism and subsequent changes.

document_title: Reserve Bank of India (Digital Lending) Directions, 2025
section: Para 6 – RE-LSP arrangements involving multiple lenders
text: The digital view must show lender name, loan amount, tenor, APR, monthly repayment obligation and applicable penal charges, with a KFS link for each offer.

document_title: Reserve Bank of India (Digital Lending) Directions, 2025
section: Para 6 – RE-LSP arrangements involving multiple lenders
text: Loan offers must be displayed in an unbiased and objective manner and must not directly or indirectly promote a particular RE through misleading or deceptive patterns.

document_title: Reserve Bank of India (Digital Lending) Directions, 2025
section: Para 6 – RE-LSP arrangements involving multiple lenders
text: A publicly pre-disclosed metric may be used to rank loan offers and, by itself, is not treated as promoting a particular product.

document_title: Reserve Bank of India (Digital Lending) Directions, 2025
text: Before extending a loan, the RE must obtain necessary information about the borrower's economic profile, including at minimum age, occupation and income details, and retain it for audit purposes.

document_title: Reserve Bank of India (Digital Lending) Directions, 2025
text: An automatic increase in a borrower's credit limit is not permitted unless the borrower explicitly requests it and the request is evaluated and recorded.

document_title: Reserve Bank of India (Digital Lending) Directions, 2025
text: The RE must provide the borrower with a Key Fact Statement in accordance with RBI's applicable KFS instructions.

document_title: Reserve Bank of India (Digital Lending) Directions, 2025
text: Applicable penal charges must follow the RBI framework on fair-lending penal charges.

document_title: Reserve Bank of India (Digital Lending) Directions, 2025
text: The KFS, loan-product summary, sanction letter, terms and conditions, account statements and relevant privacy policies must automatically be sent to the borrower's registered and verified email or SMS after execution of the relevant transaction.

document_title: Reserve Bank of India (Digital Lending) Directions, 2025
text: The RE must maintain a public, up-to-date website containing details of digital lending products and DLAs, LSPs and their DLAs, customer-care and grievance mechanisms, RBI CMS and Sachet links, and privacy-policy information.

document_title: Reserve Bank of India (Digital Lending) Directions, 2025
text: When a recovery agent is assigned or changed after a loan default, the authorised recovery agent's particulars must be communicated to the borrower by email or SMS before the agent contacts the borrower.

document_title: Reserve Bank of India (Digital Lending) Directions, 2025
section: Para 9 – Loan disbursal, servicing and repayment
text: Loan disbursal must be made to the borrower's bank account, subject to the specific statutory, regulatory, co-lending and end-use exceptions stated in the Directions.

document_title: Reserve Bank of India (Digital Lending) Directions, 2025
section: Para 9 – Loan disbursal, servicing and repayment
text: Loan servicing and repayment must be executed directly between the borrower and the RE's bank account without a third-party pass-through or pool account.

document_title: Reserve Bank of India (Digital Lending) Directions, 2025
section: Para 9 – Loan disbursal, servicing and repayment
text: The flow of funds between borrower and RE bank accounts must not be controlled directly or indirectly by a third party, including an LSP.

document_title: Reserve Bank of India (Digital Lending) Directions, 2025
section: Para 9 – Loan disbursal, servicing and repayment
text: Fees, charges and reimbursements payable to an LSP must be paid by the RE and must not be separately charged to or collected from borrowers by the LSP.

document_title: Reserve Bank of India (Digital Lending) Directions, 2025
section: Para 9 – Loan disbursal, servicing and repayment
text: For delinquent loans, physical cash recovery may be used where necessary, but the recovery must be fully reflected in the borrower's account on the same day and LSP recovery fees must be paid by the RE.

document_title: Reserve Bank of India (Digital Lending) Directions, 2025
text: The borrower must have an explicit option to exit a digital loan during the initial cooling-off period by paying principal and proportionate APR without penalty.

document_title: Reserve Bank of India (Digital Lending) Directions, 2025
text: The Board-approved loan policy determines the cooling-off period, but it cannot be less than one day; pre-payment remains available after the cooling-off period under applicable RBI requirements.

document_title: Reserve Bank of India (Digital Lending) Directions, 2025
text: The RE and an LSP that interfaces with borrowers must designate nodal grievance redressal officers for digital-lending complaints.

document_title: Reserve Bank of India (Digital Lending) Directions, 2025
text: Nodal-officer contact details must be displayed on the RE/LSP websites, DLA and KFS, and a complaint-lodging facility must be available on the DLA and website.

document_title: Reserve Bank of India (Digital Lending) Directions, 2025
text: If a complaint is rejected, the borrower is dissatisfied with the response, or no response is received within 30 days, the borrower may use RBI's CMS/RB-IOS mechanism or the prescribed physical complaint channel.

document_title: Reserve Bank of India (Digital Lending) Directions, 2025
section: Para 12 – Collection, usage and sharing of data with third parties
text: Data collected by the RE's or LSP's DLA must be need-based, obtained with prior and explicit borrower consent, and have an audit trail.

document_title: Reserve Bank of India (Digital Lending) Directions, 2025
section: Para 12 – Collection, usage and sharing of data with third parties
text: DLAs must desist from accessing phone resources such as files/media, contacts, call logs and telephony functions; one-time access to camera, microphone, location or another necessary facility is permitted for onboarding/KYC with explicit consent.

document_title: Reserve Bank of India (Digital Lending) Directions, 2025
section: Para 12 – Collection, usage and sharing of data with third parties
text: Borrowers must be able to give or deny consent for specific data uses, restrict third-party disclosure, control retention, revoke consent and, where required, request deletion/forgetting of data.

document_title: Reserve Bank of India (Digital Lending) Directions, 2025
section: Para 12 – Collection, usage and sharing of data with third parties
text: The purpose for obtaining borrower consent must be disclosed at each stage of the borrower interface.

document_title: Reserve Bank of India (Digital Lending) Directions, 2025
section: Para 12 – Collection, usage and sharing of data with third parties
text: Explicit borrower consent is required before sharing personal information with a third party, except where sharing is required by law or regulation.

document_title: Reserve Bank of India (Digital Lending) Directions, 2025
text: An LSP must not store borrower personal information except basic minimal data needed for operations or services within the RE-LSP agreement.

document_title: Reserve Bank of India (Digital Lending) Directions, 2025
text: The RE must put in place and disclose clear policies covering the type of data stored, storage duration, use restrictions, destruction protocol and security-breach handling.

document_title: Reserve Bank of India (Digital Lending) Directions, 2025
text: The RE and LSP must not store or collect biometric data unless permitted by applicable statutory guidelines.

document_title: Reserve Bank of India (Digital Lending) Directions, 2025
text: Data must be stored on servers located in India; data processed outside India must be deleted from foreign servers and brought back to India within 24 hours of processing, subject to applicable obligations.

document_title: Reserve Bank of India (Digital Lending) Directions, 2025
text: The RE and its LSPs must maintain a comprehensive privacy policy compliant with applicable laws, regulations and RBI guidelines and make it publicly available.

document_title: Reserve Bank of India (Digital Lending) Directions, 2025
text: Where applicable, the privacy policy must disclose details of third parties permitted to collect personal information through the DLA.

document_title: Reserve Bank of India (Digital Lending) Directions, 2025
text: The RE and its LSPs must comply with technology and cybersecurity standards or requirements stipulated by RBI and other relevant agencies for digital lending.

document_title: Reserve Bank of India (Digital Lending) Directions, 2025
section: Para 16 – Reporting to Credit Information Companies (CICs)
text: Lending through the RE's DLAs or LSP DLAs must be reported by the RE to CICs irrespective of the nature or tenor of the lending.

document_title: Reserve Bank of India (Digital Lending) Directions, 2025
section: Para 16 – Reporting to Credit Information Companies (CICs)
text: Structured digital lending products over merchant platforms involving short-term, unsecured/secured credit or deferred payments must be reported to CICs by the RE.

document_title: Reserve Bank of India (Digital Lending) Directions, 2025
section: Para 17 – Reporting of DLAs to RBI
text: The RE must report all DLAs it deploys or joins, including its own and LSP DLAs, to RBI's CIMS portal in the prescribed Annex I format.

document_title: Reserve Bank of India (Digital Lending) Directions, 2025
section: Para 17 – Reporting of DLAs to RBI
text: The RE must update the CIMS list when additional DLAs are deployed or engagement with an existing DLA ceases.

document_title: Reserve Bank of India (Digital Lending) Directions, 2025
section: Para 17 – Reporting of DLAs to RBI
text: The Chief Compliance Officer or Board-designated official must certify that DLA information submitted on CIMS is correct and that the DLAs comply with applicable regulatory instructions.

document_title: Reserve Bank of India (Digital Lending) Directions, 2025
section: Para 17 – Reporting of DLAs to RBI
text: The certification covers RE-website links, grievance-officer availability for LSP-owned DLAs, compliance with data collection/storage requirements, and disclosure of DLA particulars on the RE website.

document_title: Reserve Bank of India (Digital Lending) Directions, 2025
section: Para 17 – Reporting of DLAs to RBI
text: The RE is responsible for the correctness and timeliness of DLA information submitted on CIMS; RBI does not verify/validate the submitted data, and DLA-related customer grievances remain with the RE.

document_title: Reserve Bank of India (Digital Lending) Directions, 2025
text: Inclusion of a third-party DLA in RBI reporting must not be represented as RBI registration, authorisation or endorsement.

document_title: Reserve Bank of India (Digital Lending) Directions, 2025
text: Reporting of all DLAs on the CIMS portal was required to be completed by June 15, 2025.

document_title: Reserve Bank of India (Digital Lending) Directions, 2025
text: An RE may enter into a DLG arrangement only with an LSP or another RE acting as an LSP; an LSP providing DLG must be incorporated as a company under the Companies Act, 2013.

document_title: Reserve Bank of India (Digital Lending) Directions, 2025
section: Para 19 – Due diligence and other requirements with respect to DLG provider
text: An RE, including an RE acting as DLG provider, must have a Board-approved policy covering provider eligibility, nature and extent of DLG cover, monitoring/review, and applicable fees.

document_title: Reserve Bank of India (Digital Lending) Directions, 2025
section: Para 19 – Due diligence and other requirements with respect to DLG provider
text: A DLG arrangement must not substitute for credit appraisal; robust credit underwriting standards must continue to apply.
topic: DLG is not a substitute for underwriting

document_title: Reserve Bank of India (Digital Lending) Directions, 2025
section: Para 19 – Due diligence and other requirements with respect to DLG provider
text: When entering into or renewing DLG, the RE must obtain adequate information to satisfy itself that the DLG provider can honour the guarantee, including the prescribed auditor-certified declaration.

document_title: Reserve Bank of India (Digital Lending) Directions, 2025
section: Para 19 – Due diligence and other requirements with respect to DLG provider
text: The DLG-provider declaration must cover aggregate DLG outstanding, the number of REs and portfolios covered, and past default rates on similar portfolios.

document_title: Reserve Bank of India (Digital Lending) Directions, 2025
section: Para 20 – Restrictions on entering into DLG arrangements
text: REs must not enter into DLG arrangements for revolving credit facilities offered through digital lending channels or for credit cards.

document_title: Reserve Bank of India (Digital Lending) Directions, 2025
section: Para 20 – Restrictions on entering into DLG arrangements
text: REs must not enter into DLG arrangements on loans covered by the specified credit-guarantee schemes.

document_title: Reserve Bank of India (Digital Lending) Directions, 2025
section: Para 20 – Restrictions on entering into DLG arrangements
text: NBFC-P2P entities must not enter into DLG arrangements for loans facilitated over their platforms.

document_title: Reserve Bank of India (Digital Lending) Directions, 2025
text: A DLG arrangement must be backed by an explicit and legally enforceable contract specifying the extent/form of cover, invocation timeline and disclosure requirements.

document_title: Reserve Bank of India (Digital Lending) Directions, 2025
text: An RE may accept DLG only as cash deposited with the RE, a lien-marked fixed deposit with a Scheduled Commercial Bank, or a bank guarantee in favour of the RE.

document_title: Reserve Bank of India (Digital Lending) Directions, 2025
text: Total DLG cover on an outstanding portfolio specified upfront must not exceed five per cent of the total amount disbursed from that loan portfolio at any time; the same five-per-cent performance-risk limit applies to implicit guarantees.

document_title: Reserve Bank of India (Digital Lending) Directions, 2025
text: NPA recognition and provisioning remain the responsibility of the RE irrespective of DLG; invoking DLG does not reduce the borrower's underlying liability, and invoked DLG cannot be reinstated.

document_title: Reserve Bank of India (Digital Lending) Directions, 2025
text: Recoveries from loans on which DLG has been invoked may be shared with the DLG provider according to the contract.

document_title: Reserve Bank of India (Digital Lending) Directions, 2025
section: Para 25 – Treatment of DLG for regulatory capital
text: Exposure computation and credit-risk-mitigation treatment continue under applicable norms; an RE acting as DLG provider must deduct the full outstanding DLG amount from capital.

document_title: Reserve Bank of India (Digital Lending) Directions, 2025
section: Para 26 – Invocation and tenor of DLG
text: The RE must invoke DLG within a maximum overdue period of 120 days unless the borrower cures the dues earlier.

document_title: Reserve Bank of India (Digital Lending) Directions, 2025
text: LSPs with DLG arrangements must publish on their website the total number of covered portfolios and the amount of each portfolio; the RE name may or may not be disclosed.

document_title: Reserve Bank of India (Digital Lending) Directions, 2025
text: DLG portfolio disclosure must be made monthly, no later than seven working days after the end of the relevant month.

document_title: Reserve Bank of India (Digital Lending) Directions, 2025
text: Guarantees under the specified CGTMSE, CRGFTLIH and NCGTC schemes are outside the definition of DLG.

document_title: Reserve Bank of India (Digital Lending) Directions, 2025
text: EMI programmes on credit cards governed by the specified Credit Card and Debit Card Directions are outside these Directions; other credit-card loan products and loans offered on debit cards are governed as specified.

document_title: Reserve Bank of India (Digital Lending) Directions, 2025
text: Compliant DLG arrangements under Chapter VI are not treated as synthetic securitisation or loan participation under the cited RBI frameworks.

document_title: Reserve Bank of India (Digital Lending) Directions, 2025
text: The instructions and guidelines listed in Annex III are repealed upon issuance of these Directions.

document_title: Reserve Bank of India (Digital Lending) Directions, 2025
text: Actions, directions, proceedings, penalties or fines taken under repealed provisions continue to be treated as taken under the corresponding provisions of these Directions where not inconsistent with them.
The Act applies to the processing of digital personal data within India where the personal data is collected from Data Principals in India, subject to the conditions specified in the Act.
The Act also applies to processing of digital personal data outside India where such processing is in connection with offering goods or services to Data Principals in India, subject to the Act.
Before or at the time of requesting consent, the Data Fiduciary is required to give notice informing the Data Principal about the personal data proposed to be processed and the purpose of processing.
The notice should provide information required under the Act and enable the Data Principal to understand the processing for which consent is being sought.
Consent given by a Data Principal for processing personal data must be free, specific, informed and unambiguous, with a clear affirmative action.
A Data Principal may withdraw consent at any time, and withdrawal should be as easy as giving consent.
The Data Fiduciary should provide a mechanism through which a Data Principal can withdraw consent, subject to the consequences specified under the Act.
Personal data may be processed for certain legitimate uses specified in the Act, including circumstances where processing is permitted without relying on consent under Section 6.
A Data Fiduciary remains responsible for complying with the Act when processing personal data and must implement the obligations applicable to its processing activities.

A Data Fiduciary should make reasonable efforts to ensure that personal data processed by it is complete, accurate and consistent where the data is likely to be used to make a decision affecting the Data Principal or disclosed to another Data Fiduciary.
A Data Fiduciary may engage a Data Processor to process personal data on its behalf only under a valid contract.
Where personal data is likely to be used to make a decision affecting the Data Principal, the Data Fiduciary must ensure that the data is complete, accurate and consistent.
Where personal data is likely to be disclosed to another Data Fiduciary, the Data Fiduciary must ensure its completeness, accuracy and consistency.
A Data Fiduciary must implement appropriate technical and organisational measures to ensure effective observance of the Act and its rules.
A Data Fiduciary must protect personal data in its possession or control by taking reasonable security safeguards to prevent personal data breaches.
In the event of a personal data breach, the Data Fiduciary must give the Board and each affected Data Principal an intimation in the prescribed form and manner.
A Data Fiduciary must erase personal data when its retention is no longer necessary, including when the Data Principal withdraws consent, unless retention is required by law.
A Data Fiduciary must publish its business contact information and the means by which a Data Principal may contact it regarding the exercise of rights under the Act.
A Data Fiduciary must establish an effective mechanism for grievance redressal and respond to grievances within the prescribed period.
A Data Fiduciary must enable a Data Principal to nominate another individual to exercise the Data Principal's rights in accordance with the Act in the event of death or incapacity.
Before processing personal data of a child, a Data Fiduciary must obtain verifiable consent of the parent or lawful guardian in the prescribed manner.
Before processing personal data of a person with disability who has a lawful guardian, a Data Fiduciary must obtain verifiable consent of the lawful guardian in the prescribed manner.
A Data Fiduciary must not process personal data in a manner that is likely to cause a detrimental effect on the well-being of a child.
A Data Fiduciary must not undertake tracking or behavioural monitoring of children, subject to the exemptions provided under the Act.
A Data Fiduciary must not undertake targeted advertising directed at children, subject to the exemptions provided under the Act.
The obligations relating to verifiable consent and restrictions on tracking and targeted advertising may be subject to prescribed exemptions for specified classes of Data Fiduciaries or purposes.
The Central Government may notify a Data Fiduciary or class of Data Fiduciaries as a Significant Data Fiduciary based on factors specified in the Act.
A Significant Data Fiduciary must appoint a Data Protection Officer who represents it under the Act and serves as the point of contact for the prescribed data-protection responsibilities.
A Significant Data Fiduciary must appoint an independent data auditor to carry out data audits in accordance with the Act and applicable rules.
A Significant Data Fiduciary must undertake periodic Data Protection Impact Assessments and other measures specified under the Act and applicable rules.
A Data Principal has the right to obtain information about the personal data being processed and other information relating to its processing, subject to the Act.
The right to access includes information about the personal data being processed and the manner in which the personal data is being processed, as provided by the Act.
A Data Principal has the right to correction, completion and updating of personal data in accordance with the provisions of the Act.
A Data Principal has the right to erasure of personal data that is no longer necessary for the purpose for which it was processed, subject to the applicable provisions of the Act.
A Data Principal has the right to grievance redressal in respect of any act or omission by a Data Fiduciary concerning the performance of its obligations under the Act.
A Data Principal should use the grievance redressal mechanism established by the Data Fiduciary before exercising the right to approach the Board, subject to the conditions specified in the Act.
A Data Principal has the right to nominate another individual to exercise the rights of the Data Principal in accordance with the Act in the event of death or incapacity.
A Data Principal is required to comply with the duties specified under the Act while exercising rights and interacting with Data Fiduciaries.
A Data Principal should provide authentic information while exercising the right to correction or updating of personal data.
A Data Principal should not register a false or frivolous grievance or complaint with a Data Fiduciary or the Board.
The Central Government may exempt specified classes of Data Fiduciaries or processing activities from specified provisions of the Act in the circumstances provided under the Act.

Specified provisions of the Act do not apply to processing of personal data by a court, tribunal or other body where such processing is necessary for performing judicial, quasi-judicial, regulatory, supervisory or similar functions.
Specified provisions of the Act may not apply to processing necessary for prevention, detection, investigation or prosecution of offences or contraventions, subject to the conditions in the Act.

Specified provisions may not apply to processing necessary for research, archiving or statistical purposes where the personal data is not used to make a decision specific to a Data Principal and the prescribed standards are followed.

The Central Government may notify certain Data Fiduciaries, including eligible start-ups, to whom specified provisions of the Act do not apply, having regard to the volume and nature of personal data processed.
The Act provides for establishment of a Data Protection Board of India for carrying out the purposes of the Act.
The Data Protection Board consists of a Chairperson and such number of other Members as may be notified by the Central Government.
The Chairperson and other Members of the Data Protection Board hold office for the term prescribed under the Act and are eligible for re-appointment subject to the applicable provisions.
The Act specifies the circumstances and procedure relating to resignation and removal of the Chairperson or other Members of the Data Protection Board.
The Data Protection Board exercises the powers and performs the functions assigned to it under the Act, including dealing with matters relating to personal data breaches and compliance.
The Central Government may establish the Data Protection Board of India as a body corporate for carrying out the purposes of the Act.

section: Section 24 – Qualifications of Chairperson and Members
text: The Chairperson and Members of the Data Protection Board must satisfy the qualifications and other conditions prescribed under the Act.
The salary, allowances and other terms and conditions of service of the Chairperson and Members of the Board are governed by the provisions specified under the Act.
The Chairperson exercises general superintendence and gives directions regarding the administrative matters of the Data Protection Board.
The Chairperson may authorise Members or groups of Members to perform functions and conduct proceedings of the Board and may allocate proceedings among them.
On receiving an intimation of a personal data breach, the Board may direct urgent remedial or mitigation measures, inquire into the breach and impose penalties as provided under the Act.
The Board may inquire into complaints concerning breaches of a Data Fiduciary's obligations or infringement of a Data Principal's rights and may impose penalties as provided under the Act.
After giving the concerned person an opportunity of being heard and recording reasons in writing, the Board may issue directions necessary for effective discharge of its functions.
The Data Protection Board functions as an independent body and, as far as practicable, operates as a digital office for receiving complaints and conducting proceedings.
The Board may take action on intimations, complaints, references or directions in accordance with the Act and the rules made under it.
A person aggrieved by an order or direction of the Data Protection Board may appeal against the order or direction before the Appellate Tribunal in accordance with the Act.
The Act provides for consequences where a person fails to comply with an order or direction of the Data Protection Board, including the consequences specified under the Act.
The Data Protection Board may impose penalties for breaches of the provisions of the Act after following the procedure prescribed under the Act.
The Schedule specifies financial penalties that may be imposed for specified breaches of obligations under the Act.
Failure by a Data Fiduciary to take reasonable security safeguards to prevent personal data breaches may attract a penalty as specified in the Schedule.
Failure to notify the Board or affected Data Principals of a personal data breach as required by the Act may attract a penalty specified in the Schedule.
Breaches of the obligations relating to children's personal data may attract the financial penalty specified in the Schedule.
Breach of applicable obligations relating to Data Principal rights may attract consequences under the Act, including penalties where specified in the Schedule.
Failure by a Significant Data Fiduciary to comply with applicable obligations may attract penalties as specified under the Act and its Schedule.
The Schedule provides for penalties that may extend to the specified maximum amounts for the corresponding breaches of obligations under the Act.

A notice given by a Data Fiduciary to a Data Principal should be presented independently and should provide clear information about the personal data being collected and the purpose for processing it.
The notice should provide an itemised description of the personal data being collected from the Data Principal.
The notice should provide an itemised description of the purposes for which the personal data is proposed to be processed.
The notice should provide an itemised description of the goods, services or uses enabled by the processing of personal data.
The notice should provide a communication link or other mechanism through which a Data Principal can withdraw consent as easily as consent was given.
The notice should provide information about the means through which a Data Principal can exercise the rights available under the Act.
The notice should provide information about the means through which a Data Principal can make a complaint to the Data Fiduciary or the Data Protection Board, as applicable.
A Consent Manager must be incorporated in India and meet the eligibility and registration requirements prescribed under the Rules.
A registered Consent Manager is required to maintain records relating to consents given, managed, reviewed or withdrawn by Data Principals in accordance with the Rules.
A Consent Manager should provide Data Principals with an interoperable platform through which they can give, manage, review and withdraw consent.

A Data Fiduciary may process personal data for providing or issuing subsidies, benefits, services, certificates, licences or permits by the State or its instrumentalities, subject to the conditions specified in the Rules.
Processing of personal data for specified State services must be carried out in accordance with applicable law and the standards prescribed under the Rules.
Personal data processed for State services should be limited to what is necessary for the specified purpose for which it is processed.
Personal data processed for the specified State services should be maintained with appropriate accuracy and completeness.
Personal data processed for the specified State services should be retained only for the period necessary for the applicable purpose, subject to legal requirements.
Appropriate technical and organisational measures should be implemented to protect personal data processed for the specified State services.
Data Principals should be provided appropriate information about processing and the means available to exercise their rights under the Act.
A Data Fiduciary must implement reasonable security safeguards to prevent personal data breaches, including appropriate technical and organisational measures.
Security measures may include encryption, obfuscation or masking, access controls, logging and monitoring, backups, and measures for detecting and responding to unauthorised access.
Contracts between a Data Fiduciary and Data Processor should require the Data Processor to implement appropriate security safeguards for personal data processed on behalf of the Data Fiduciary.
On becoming aware of a personal data breach, the Data Fiduciary should notify each affected Data Principal without delay in the manner specified under the Rules.
The Data Fiduciary should notify the Data Protection Board of India of a personal data breach in the manner and within the timeline prescribed under the Rules.
The breach notification should contain the information required under the Rules concerning the nature and circumstances of the personal data breach.
A Data Fiduciary should communicate appropriate information about measures taken or proposed to mitigate the effects of a personal data breach.
A Data Fiduciary should publish its business contact information and provide an appropriate means for Data Principals to communicate regarding their personal data and rights.
The published contact information should enable Data Principals to contact the Data Fiduciary regarding processing of their personal data and exercise of their rights.
A Data Fiduciary processing the personal data of a child should obtain verifiable consent from the parent in accordance with the requirements prescribed by the Rules.
The Data Fiduciary should take reasonable measures to verify that the individual providing consent is an identifiable adult who is the parent of the child.
A Significant Data Fiduciary is required to undertake the additional governance, security and compliance measures prescribed under the Rules.
A Significant Data Fiduciary should undertake periodic Data Protection Impact Assessments and audits in accordance with the requirements prescribed under the Act and Rules.

A Data Fiduciary obtaining verifiable consent from a person identifying herself as the lawful guardian of a person with disability must conduct due diligence to verify that the guardian was appointed by a court, designated authority, or local level committee under the applicable guardianship law.

The Rules define the applicable guardianship framework for persons with disabilities, including the Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act, 2016 and the National Trust Act, 1999, depending on the person's circumstances.

The Rules define a person with disability for the purpose of obtaining verifiable consent through a lawful guardian, including specified disabilities where the person is unable to take legally binding decisions despite adequate and appropriate support.

Certain obligations under section 9 of the DPDP Act do not apply to processing personal data of a child by classes of Data Fiduciaries specified in Part A of the Fourth Schedule, subject to the conditions in that Schedule.

Certain obligations under section 9 of the DPDP Act do not apply to processing personal data of a child for purposes specified in Part B of the Fourth Schedule, subject to the conditions specified there.

A Significant Data Fiduciary must undertake a Data Protection Impact Assessment and an audit once every twelve months from the date it is notified as a Significant Data Fiduciary or included in a notified class.

The person carrying out the Data Protection Impact Assessment and audit for a Significant Data Fiduciary must furnish the Board with a report containing significant observations from the DPIA and audit.

A Significant Data Fiduciary must conduct due diligence to verify that technical measures, including algorithmic software used for processing personal data, are not likely to pose a risk to the rights of Data Principals.

A Significant Data Fiduciary must take measures to ensure that personal data specified by the Central Government is processed subject to restrictions preventing the specified personal data and related traffic data from being transferred outside India.
Data Fiduciaries and, where applicable, Consent Managers must prominently publish on their website or app the means through which Data Principals may request exercise of their rights under the Act.
The published information must include particulars such as a username or other identifier that may be required to identify the Data Principal under the Data Fiduciary's terms of service.
A Data Principal may exercise rights under the Act by making a request to the Data Fiduciary to whom she previously gave consent, using the means and particulars required by that Data Fiduciary.
Every Data Fiduciary and Consent Manager must prominently publish its grievance redressal system and respond to Data Principal grievances within a reasonable period not exceeding ninety days.
A Data Principal may nominate one or more individuals to exercise her rights under the Act, subject to the terms of service of the Data Fiduciary and applicable law.

Personal data processed by a Data Fiduciary under the DPDP Act may be transferred outside the territory of India subject to requirements that the Central Government may specify regarding making such personal data available to a foreign State or persons or entities under the control of or agencies of such a State.

The provisions of the DPDP Act do not apply to processing of personal data necessary for research, archiving or statistical purposes when such processing is carried out in accordance with the standards specified in the Second Schedule.
The Central Government shall constitute a Search-cum-Selection Committee to recommend individuals for appointment as Chairperson of the Data Protection Board.
The Central Government shall constitute a Search-cum-Selection Committee to recommend individuals for appointment as Members of the Data Protection Board other than the Chairperson.
The Central Government shall appoint the Chairperson or other Members after considering the suitability of the individuals recommended by the respective Search-cum-Selection Committee.
The Chairperson and other Members of the Data Protection Board shall be paid such salary, allowances and other terms and conditions of service as specified in the Fifth Schedule.
The salary, allowances and other service conditions of the Chairperson and Members are subject to the provisions specified in the Fifth Schedule.
The Chairperson shall preside over meetings of the Data Protection Board.
The Chairperson shall determine the date, time and place of meetings of the Data Protection Board.
The Chairperson shall determine the agenda for meetings of the Data Protection Board.
In the absence of the Chairperson, a Member chosen by the Members present shall preside over the meeting of the Data Protection Board.
The quorum for a meeting of the Data Protection Board shall be one-third of the total number of Members of the Board.

Questions arising at a meeting of the Data Protection Board shall be decided by a majority of votes of the Members present and voting, and the Chairperson shall have a casting vote in the event of an equality of votes.
The proceedings of meetings of the Data Protection Board shall be recorded and maintained in the manner specified by the Board.
The Data Protection Board shall function as a digital office and use techno-legal measures to conduct its proceedings without requiring the physical presence of persons.

The Data Protection Board may, with the previous approval of the Central Government, appoint such officers and employees as it considers necessary for the efficient discharge of its functions under the DPDP Act.
topic: Data Protection Board; Officers and Employees

text: The terms and conditions of service of officers and employees of the Data Protection Board are specified in the Sixth Schedule to the Rules.
Rule 21 requires prior approval of the Central Government before the Data Protection Board appoints officers or employees necessary for carrying out its functions.
The service conditions applicable to officers and employees appointed by the Data Protection Board are governed by the Sixth Schedule.

Rule 21 concerns the appointment and service conditions of officers and employees of the Data Protection Board and does not itself specify additional categories of employees or separate appointment mechanisms.

Any person aggrieved by an order or direction of the Data Protection Board may prefer an appeal before the Appellate Tribunal, and the appeal shall be filed in digital form as the Appellate Tribunal may decide.

An appeal before the Appellate Tribunal must be accompanied by a fee of the amount applicable to an appeal under the Telecom Regulatory Authority of India Act, 1997, unless the fee is reduced or waived by the Chairperson of the Appellate Tribunal. The fee is payable digitally using UPI or another payment system authorised by the Reserve Bank of India.

The Appellate Tribunal is not bound by the procedure under the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908, is guided by principles of natural justice, may regulate its own procedure subject to the Act, and functions as a digital office using techno-legal measures.
topic: Appellate Tribunal; Natural Justice; Digital Office

text: The Central Government may, for purposes of the Act specified in the Seventh Schedule and through the corresponding authorised person specified there, require a Data Fiduciary or intermediary to furnish information within the specified period.

Where disclosure or furnishing of information is likely to prejudicially affect the sovereignty and integrity of India or security of the State, the Central Government may require the Data Fiduciary or intermediary not to disclose the furnishing of such information without prior written permission of the authorised person.
For the purposes of Rule 23, intermediary has the same meaning as assigned to it under the Information Technology Act, 2000.

document_title: Securities and Exchange Board of India (Investment Advisers) Regulations, 2013
text: On and from the commencement of these regulations, no person shall act as or hold itself out as an investment adviser unless it has obtained a certificate of registration from SEBI, subject to applicable exemptions.

document_title: Securities and Exchange Board of India (Investment Advisers) Regulations, 2013
text: An investment adviser shall obtain necessary information from the client relevant to providing investment advice, including the client's age, investment objectives, income details, existing investments and risk appetite, and shall carry out risk profiling of the client.

document_title: Securities and Exchange Board of India (Investment Advisers) Regulations, 2013
text: An investment adviser shall ensure that all investment advice given to a client, and any product recommended, is suitable to the risk profile of the client.

document_title: Securities and Exchange Board of India (Investment Advisers) Regulations, 2013
text: Suitability requires the investment adviser to have reasonable grounds to believe that a recommendation is suitable for the client on the basis of information furnished by the client about their financial situation, investment objectives and risk tolerance.

document_title: Securities and Exchange Board of India (Investment Advisers) Regulations, 2013
text: An investment adviser must exercise due skill, care and diligence in recommending complex or high-risk products and must take into account the client's investment experience before doing so.

document_title: Securities and Exchange Board of India (Investment Advisers) Regulations, 2013
text: Regulation 15 sets out general obligations of investment advisers, including a requirement to maintain confidentiality of client information and not disclose it to any other person or entity except with client consent or as required by law.

document_title: Securities and Exchange Board of India (Investment Advisers) Regulations, 2013
text: Under the general obligations in Regulation 15, an investment adviser is required to comply with applicable Know Your Client (KYC) requirements specified by SEBI before providing investment advisory services to a client.

document_title: Securities and Exchange Board of India (Investment Advisers) Regulations, 2013
text: An investment adviser shall maintain records of know-your-client, risk profiling, suitability assessment, and the basis on which investment advice was given, for the period specified by SEBI.

document_title: Securities and Exchange Board of India (Investment Advisers) Regulations, 2013
text: Records maintained under Regulation 19 must be made available to SEBI as and when required, including records relating to client interactions and the rationale for recommendations, so compliance can be verified.

document_title: Securities and Exchange Board of India (Investment Advisers) Regulations, 2013
text: General obligations under Regulation 15 require an investment adviser to act in a fiduciary capacity, disclose all material information including actual or potential conflicts of interest, and not receive any consideration by way of remuneration from any entity other than the client without prior disclosure.

document_title: Securities and Exchange Board of India (Investment Advisers) Regulations, 2013
text: Where an investment adviser or an associated person receives any consideration for distribution or execution of a product recommended to a client, this must be disclosed to the client as a conflict of interest before the advice is acted upon.

document_title: Securities and Exchange Board of India (Investment Advisers) Regulations, 2013
text: Where an investment adviser uses artificial intelligence or machine-learning tools in providing investment advisory services, the adviser remains responsible for the output, quality and suitability of any advice generated, and must disclose the use of such tools to clients.

document_title: Securities and Exchange Board of India (Investment Advisers) Regulations, 2013
text: Disclosure requirements under Regulation 18 extend to informing clients, prior to providing advice, where advisory services or systems (including AI/ML-based tools) are involved, so clients can make an informed decision about the advice being relied upon.

document_title: Securities and Exchange Board of India (Investment Advisers) Regulations, 2013
text: Investment advisers that are banks, NBFCs or body corporates providing distribution or execution services must keep their investment advisory services segregated from such other activities, including at the client level.
Securities markets cannot offer assured or guaranteed returns; any entity or scheme promising fixed, assured or unusually high returns should be treated as a red flag for potential fraud.

Even SEBI-registered portfolio managers and investment advisers are not permitted to offer products with guaranteed or assured returns; investors should verify an entity's registration status directly on the SEBI website before relying on any return claims.
Investments in securities are subject to market risk; there is no guarantee of returns, and the value of an investment can rise or fall depending on market conditions.
Investors are encouraged to understand the features, risks and costs of an investment option, including its liquidity, tenure and past performance, before making an investment decision.

Collection of data by digital lending apps must be need-based, carried out with the borrower's prior and explicit consent, and must have an audit trail; apps must not access mobile resources such as contact lists, call logs or media files beyond what is required for onboarding or KYC.

The regulated entity and its lending service providers must provide borrowers with a clear and accessible privacy policy explaining what data is collected, how it is used, and with whom it may be shared.
Regulated entities must ensure a comprehensive assessment of the borrower's creditworthiness, including their economic profile, before extending any digital credit facility.

The Key Fact Statement must be provided to the borrower before execution of the loan contract and must disclose the all-inclusive annual percentage rate (APR), recovery mechanism, and any applicable penal charges upfront on an annualised basis.

All loan disbursals and repayments must be executed directly between the bank accounts of the borrower and the regulated entity, without routing through any pass-through or pool account operated by a lending service provider or other third party.

Disbursal of the sanctioned digital loan must be made directly into the borrower's bank account; disbursal into an account operated by a lending service provider or app is not permitted, except in specifically permitted co-lending or end-use disbursal scenarios.

Repayment of a digital loan, including any charges or penal interest, must be collected directly by the regulated entity into its own bank account and must not be routed through a third-party pooling arrangement.
Borrowers must be given an explicit cooling-off or look-up period during which they may exit a digital loan by paying the principal and the proportionate APR without incurring any penalty.
Where recovery of a digital loan is outsourced, the borrower must be informed of the name and contact details of the recovery agent authorised to approach them before recovery activity begins.

Regulated entities and their lending service providers must maintain an effective grievance redressal mechanism for digital lending, with a nodal grievance redressal officer whose contact details are prominently displayed on the entity's website, its LSPs' websites and the lending app.
